claim: For every finite ordinal \(n<\omega\), the ordinal-indexed fixed-point proof system \(\mu\mathrm{MALL}_{n,n}\) has an effective finite translation to ordinary MALL preserving provability, uniformly in \(n\); hence the combined finite-stage theoremhood problem is decidable. At the first infinite stage \(\alpha=\omega\), theoremhood is \(\Sigma^0_{\omega^{\omega^\omega}}\)-complete under Turing reductions.

correctness.rationale: For finite beta, both indexed premise families are finite. The mu rule is simulated by finite additive disjunction and the nu rule by finite additive conjunction. The translation terminates by induction on finite annotations and syntax, preserves derivability in both directions, and reduces theoremhood uniformly to decidable MALL proof search. The \(\alpha=\omega\) complexity value is the exact specialization of Theorem 2.8 in the cited primary paper.

value.rationale: The result completes a mathematically natural boundary: finite ordinal annotations can be eliminated effectively, while the first infinite stage has a hyperarithmetically complete theoremhood problem. The cutoff is structural—the greatest-fixed-point rule changes from finitely many premises to infinitely many—not an arbitrary numerical slice.
